coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: No search spent: K03 already covers the household carer-employer paperwork and the budget went to unscreened categories. Jobsplus 2025-26 TCN rules (Labour Market Test mandatory from Oct 2025, Pre-Departure Course from Jan 2026) surfaced incidentally under category 15; they support K01/K03 but are not a new buyer group.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No separate scrap dealer licence found. Scrap and ELV dealing sits under ERA waste permits (EP permits, permitted-sites list on era.org.mt) and enforcement orders for metals/WEEE/ELV storage without permits. Permit holders are a handful of mid-size firms, not a quiet long tail. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No police second-hand dealer or pawnbroker register found in search results (unverified either way). Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Dealers in precious metals and stones need a licence under the Trading Licences Regulations SL441.07 (in force for dealers after 1 Jan 2021), via the trade licences portal (commerce.gov.mt FAQ). Mainly an AML-driven one-off licence plus change notifications; no recurring flow found. Assay Office hallmarking not found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: ELV dismantlers hold ERA permits under SL 549.36 (LN 99 of 2004). Transport Malta de-registers vehicles only against a certificate of destruction from an approved facility; the facility list is short (e.g. Gasparell Baling Plant). Very few buyers; nothing new.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Keepers of bovines, pigs and small ruminants must keep holding registers and report movements (LN 292 of 2005; pigs rules LN 346 of 2015, shown as repealed in FAOLEX, current status unverified). Herd is small; the regulator runs the traceability database. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: The Public Abattoir is the only provider of slaughter for bovines, swine, equines and small ruminants. Open data portal publishes a register of licensed slaughterline butchers. Tiny, centralised market; nothing new.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: 272 registered beekeepers (69 Gozo, 203 Malta) per a Jan 2023 parliamentary reply; about 5,595 hives (2021). Too small to support a product.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary Pharmacy Regulations 2024 (records of retail sale, Part X of Cap. 437, Art 103 of Reg 2019/6) and an electronic veterinary prescription access application exist (vsd.gov.mt). The guideline PDF returned 403, so reporting frequency and duties are unverified. Pet boarding/sitting (LN 149 of 2024) and grooming (SL 439.25) establishments also have annual registration.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: About 8,000 boreholes registered (1997 and 2008 schemes); LN 241 requires meters, yet metering stopped after about 2,900 agricultural and 245 industrial boreholes. A green paper proposed groundwater pricing. Whether pricing or a new permit regime was adopted is unverified (MaltaToday fetch blocked).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: ERA requires vehicles that carry waste to be registered, renewable yearly, and waste brokers must register annually. No septic or cesspit-specific regime found in results.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Inspection of Lifts Regulations (LN 231 of 2007, SL 427.63): residential lifts need a preventive inspection at least yearly, workplace lifts every six months. The responsible person (owner or condominium administrator) must send the inspection report to MCCAA within 28 days. Lifts are registered with MCCAA; inspections are by authorised bodies (ACABs). No reminder software found. No Maltese pressure-equipment regime found.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: No search spent; Malta is supplied by the Water Services Corporation, so private small supplies are likely marginal.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Plant protection rules: LN 284 of 2011 under Cap. 430 and LN 115 of 2004 (professional users, dealers). Distributors are certified by MCCAA. EU Implementing Reg 2023/564 requires electronic usage records, which Reg 2025/2203 lets states defer to 1 Jan 2027. Malta's use of the deferral is unverified. No fertiliser rules found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Employment Agencies Regulations 2023 (LN 270 of 2023) took effect 1 Apr or 1 Jun 2024 (sources differ). Licensed by DIER via a web portal; fee €3,000 first, €1,500 renewal; bank guarantee €20,000+; renew at least two months before expiry. Recurring reporting duties not confirmed. BDO and Mifsud Advocates publish advisory notes.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No 2025-26 funeral or cemetery rules found. Cremation law passed in 2019, but operating rules were reported as missing. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Enrolled voluntary organisations file annual returns and accounts with the Commissioner for Voluntary Organisations (SL 492.01): income under €50k within 3 months of year end on a simple template, €50k-250k within 6 months with an accountant-signed set. Administrator lists must be given in Excel and PDF. Thresholds differ between sources. No private software found; free state templates exist. Halal and kosher supervision not found.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: From 29 July 2026 Transport Malta runs LPTV1 (1-4 vehicles), LPTV2 (5+) and SOV light passenger licences (LN 171 and 172 of 2026). Licences renew annually. Rules include a 1:1 vehicle-to-driver ratio, a six-penalty-point driver cap, garaging, driving and rest periods, and booking-platform rules. Road Haulage Operator Licence is valid for 5 years. The Transport Malta pages returned 403 on fetch.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Street hawkers hold a Trade Licensing Unit licence under SL 441.07. Market hawkers need Local Council authorisation. Personal licences, with notification of stopping and substitute appointments. Fragmented and low value. Money changers not searched (unverified).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Tattoo and piercing studios and artists are licensed by the Health Care Standards Directorate under Cap 270 and SL 465.07. Childcare centres for 0-3 year olds are licensed by DQSE for 3 years, with yearly compliance checks and external evaluation. Driving instructors hold Transport Malta permits. Small food producers and driving school operators found nothing. Hunting is covered by K07.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: My own judgement, not searched: Malta is a small island state with no meaningful grain, coffee or cocoa trading, milling or warehousing sector.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: One search returned only the general MBR company annual return regime (42 days from anniversary date). No co-operative-specific statute or register was found, so the Co-operative Societies Registrar's duties are unchecked; buyer pool is likely tiny.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Search returned only old or general sources. No e-claims system or periodic reporting duty found for private clinics. Nothing found; Health Ministry licensing details unchecked.

coverage.found: Over 200 licensed community pharmacies. The managing pharmacist must send controlled-drug prescriptions to the Superintendent of Public Health monthly (SL 101.02, per a 2017 article, so possibly outdated). No precursor source found. Pharmacies likely already use pharmacy management software (unchecked).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Jobsplus employment licences: labour market testing guidelines updated August 2025 and a banner about updated licence fees. No security-services or cleaning-contractor licence source found. Close to K01 (TCN permits).

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: OHSA construction notification applies only to larger sites (over 30 working days with 20+ workers, or 500+ person-days), filed on Servizz four weeks before start. New site regulations S.L. 646.27 reportedly in force 7 Sept 2025. LN 118/2026 'Construction (Conditions of Work) Regulation Order, 2026' exists but its content was not read. BCA contractor licensing is K06 (rejected). No site register found.

result.competitor: I found no dedicated compliance software for LPTV operators. Yipii (Swieqi; fleet tracking since 2009) claims "Y-plate compliance, Transport Malta reporting" on LinkedIn, but this is vendor marketing and I did not verify it. Driving-hour monitoring seems to be done on the platform side: Transport Malta takes the data from Bolt, Uber and eCabs, which removes the most software-heavy part of the job. Transport Malta itself uses downloadable forms (LPTS 001, 005, 006, 007) plus its online licensing. Generic fleet and tachograph tools such as Frotcom and Michelin exist but do not fit Y-plate cabs.
result.duty: Real and in force. Legal Notice 171 of 2026, the Light Passenger Transport Services and Vehicle Hire Services (Amendment) Regulations 2026, was published in Government Gazette No. 21,655 on 29.05.2026 and amends S.L. 499.68. Legal Notice 172 of 2026 amends S.L. 499.56, which covers vehicles with more than 9 seats, so it does not apply to Y-plates. Transport Malta's page lists the changes from 29 July 2026: LPTV1 (1-4 vehicles), LPTV2 (5 or more) and SOV categories; garaging and off-street parking, with a 2-year minimum lease for LPTV1; a parking-clock rule with a €500 administrative fine; driver and Driver Permit Tag requirements; driving and rest periods; and administrative penalties. Some requirements apply at once and others have transition periods. I could not read the exact transitional deadlines or the rest-period and record-keeping text: the Transport Malta pages returned 403 and the LN PDF had no readable text. Search summaries of a MaltaToday report (undated) say there is a 12-hour daily driving limit, fines of up to €500 plus tag suspension, and that Transport Malta will get data from the ride-hailing platforms to monitor hours. The operator files form LPTS 005 (changes, €50 per vehicle removed) and LPTS 001/006 (renewal). Enforcement is heavy: according to a 22 July 2026 parliamentary reply, 96 Y-plate operators faced suspension, revocation or investigation between February and May 2026.
result.market: Close to 5,000 Y-plate vehicles (the minister's figure given to Parliament in November 2023), 456 of them in Gozo by March 2024. I found no count of LPTV1 operators or licences, so this is not_reached. Estimate: low thousands of licensees at most, many of them single-vehicle owner-drivers. Malta is a very small market.
result.reason: The duty is real and new (LN 171/2026, from 29 July 2026) and enforcement is aggressive, so pain is high for a short period. But the recurring obligation is mostly an annual renewal plus occasional change notifications on Transport Malta forms. Driving-hour monitoring appears to rely on platform data that goes to Transport Malta, which takes away the most valuable software piece. The market is tiny (about 5,000 vehicles, an unknown and probably low-thousands number of operators, many of them price-sensitive owner-drivers). A Maltese fleet vendor (Yipii) reportedly already markets Y-plate compliance. Transitional deadlines and rest-record rules were not read (403 errors). A done-for-you licence and paperwork service through accountants or garages is more plausible than SaaS. Limited upside for a solo founder.

Duty confirmed via search results: LN 231/2007 (SL 427.63) requires a yearly preventive inspection for residential lifts and every six months for workplace lifts. Lifts must be registered with MCCAA, and a thorough examination is required every 10 years. I found no Maltese lift-compliance software. Bexel (UK LOLER) and Property Inspect (South African) are foreign and not a fit. Not checked: penalties (the FAQ PDF was unreadable), the 28-day reporting rule, and lift or administrator counts. The data.gov.mt Lifts Register exists, but I did not open it. Pain is real because 60% of residential lifts were non-compliant in 2013. Willingness to pay is likely low, the market is small (Malta only), and lift maintenance firms and ACABs likely offer reminders themselves.

Duty is real: S.L. 492.01 requires enrolled VOs to file annual returns, 3 months after year-end under €50k and 6 months for €50k-250k (the latter with full GAPSME accounts signed by an external accountant). Confirmed via the cvo.gov.mt search listing and its snippets. I did not open the page itself (the fetch returned 404), and I found no penalty text. The state offers free templates and an online form, which is then printed and signed. I found no dedicated private software, but the market is small: about 1,300+ enrolled VOs (NAO, 2018, so dated). Buyers are volunteers with little money to spend, and accountants cover the larger ones. Pain is low and willingness to pay is low. Only one filing a year per body.

EU duty is real: Reg 2023/564 requires professional users to keep PPP use records and transfer them to electronic format within 30 days, from 1 Jan 2026. Reg 2025/2203 (31 Oct 2025) lets states defer to 1 Jan 2027. I found no Maltese source saying whether Malta deferred, who collects records, or the penalty. No Maltese competitor found, though generic EU apps exist (e.g. Farmable). The market is mostly part-time farmers (about 14,000 registered, under 10% full-time; older figures), so willingness to pay is low and the base is tiny and hard to reach. Records appear to be kept by the farmer for inspection, not submitted, which weakens the pull. Score stays at 3.

A metering duty exists under 2010 regulations. Meter fees are about 765 euro for installation and 143 euro a year per source, and the state meters and reads. Licensing and volumetric pricing are only a 2023-24 Green Paper. I found no sign it became law. Agricultural users would keep free quotas. The state or the Energy and Water Agency reads the meters, so owners have little to declare. I ran no competitor search, only two general ones. About 8,058 registered boreholes, but many are unmetered or unregistered. Buyers are mostly farmers with low willingness to pay and no recurring filing workflow. Weak case; the score stays at 3.

An FSSA reminder (Italpress, 27 Jun 2026) says traders must register and notify 48 hours before importing food, feed, animals or plants, including from the EU. The legal basis is L.N. 315 of 2004, but I could not confirm it is in force. LEAP lists it as repealed, and the FAOLEX PDF was unreadable. I found no penalties, no FSSA portal or form, no competing vendor, and no count of traders. The duty is probably an email or form to a free state channel. It is per consignment, so it recurs, but a vendor can add little on top of it. The buyer group is fragmented and has little willingness to pay. Overlap with customs and TRACES is unchecked. The score stays low.
